welcome.kicker: NASA Space Apps 2026 · Adapting Farms with NASA Data
welcome.h1: Test your next crop rotation before you plant it.
welcome.lead: FarmSmart runs your field through 35 years of real weather and shows which rotations protect your soil, save water and pay, with the risk in plain words.
welcome.trust2: Open data from NASA, USDA and NOAA
welcome.trust3: Supports your judgment, never replaces it
welcome.photo_credit: Aerial photo: USDA NAIP, Story County, Iowa
welcome.ben_h: Answers to the questions behind every rotation decision
welcome.b1_p: See how much soil each rotation loses to rain and wind, and the weeks your field sits bare.
welcome.b2_p: Crop water use from a day-by-day simulation, checked against NASA satellite water-use readings.
welcome.b3_h: Know the money and the risk
welcome.b3_p: Revenue, costs and the chance of a bad year, from real prices, your own numbers and crop-insurance records.
welcome.b4_h: Plan for droughts and the decades ahead
welcome.b4_p: Replay any dry year since 1991, and see where your 2040s climate is found today.
welcome.ex_p: This field in Story County, Iowa grows corn and soybeans today. FarmSmart tested every option it could grow against every weather year since 1991. Here is what it found for the farmer's priorities.
welcome.ex_caption: Current rotation compared with the best option for this farmer
welcome.ex_note: Typical (median) year over 35 simulated weather years. Live from FarmSmart's model for this field.
welcome.data_h: Satellites, soil maps and 35 years of weather, for your field
welcome.data_p: Every number in FarmSmart comes from public data or a model run on it, with a button that shows its source, date and scale.
welcome.proof_weather: agreement of NASA POWER daily temperatures with ground weather stations
welcome.proof_yield: of real county yields fell inside FarmSmart's 80% ranges in years it had not seen
welcome.proof_conf: of 'High confidence' ranges held the real value ({{n}} county-years)
welcome.cta_p: Start with your farm. It takes about a minute to find your field.

plan.title: Action plan · {{name}}

check.adviser: Talk the plan through with your agronomist, extension office or adviser
check.buyer: Confirm a buyer, a delivery point or an on-farm use for every new crop
check.insurance: Check crop insurance, contracts and programme rules for the new rotation
check.budget: Check the numbers with your own prices and costs (My Field → own prices)
check.soil_test: Take a recent soil test (pH, P, K) for this field
check.herbicide: Check herbicide carry-over labels from last season before each new crop
check.seed: Order seed and cover-crop seed early for the varieties that suit your area
check.equipment: Check the drill, planter and harvest settings each new crop needs
check.dates: Set planting, cover-crop seeding and termination dates with your local calendar
check.strip: Try it small first: a strip or part of the field next to your usual rotation
check.stand: Record emergence, stand and weeds in the trial and the check strip
check.cover_end: Note how the cover crop established and when and how it was ended
check.records: Keep yields, costs and field passes so you can compare at harvest
check.review: Review the results with your adviser before scaling up

plan.notes_help: Notes for you and your adviser (questions, local knowledge, decisions)

val.title: How well does it work?
val.sub: Checks of the models and data behind FarmSmart against outcomes they did not see. Numbers come from the project's validation reports.
val.missing_body: This check's report was not found on the server.
val.conf_rule: Shown as high when held-out coverage meets the 80% target, medium within 10 points of it, low otherwise.
val.m2_title: County yields on years the model never saw (M2)
val.m2_model: M2 county yield model (LightGBM quantiles, conformalized)
val.m2_help: Each line is one held-out county-year ({{years}}): the model's P10–P90 range drawn at the yield USDA NASS later reported. A line that crosses the dashed diagonal held the actual yield.
val.m2_inside: {{n}} of {{m}} ranges held the reported yield ({{p}}).
val.m2_aria: Held-out county yields: {{n}} of {{m}} P10–P90 ranges held the reported yield.
val.cov_reason: {{crop}}: 80% ranges held the yield {{p}} of the time ({{years}})
val.cov_target: Coverage of the 80% range per crop; the navy mark is the 80% target.
val.no_points: No held-out points were returned for this crop.
val.m10_title: Do the confidence labels mean what they say? (M10)
val.m10_model: M10 uncertainty labels (rules on range width and inputs)
val.m10_help: How often each confidence level's 80% range held the reported county yield on held-out years. A level is honest when it is close to 80%.
val.wx_title: NASA POWER weather vs ground stations
val.wx_help: POWER is a regional value (≈50 km) and a station is one point. Correlation (r) of daily and monthly values over the comparison period.
val.wx_read: Temperature and monthly rain agree well. Single-day rain agrees less because storms are local, which is why daily rain is labelled regional.
val.m3_help: Held-out year: how often the model's first guess, or one of its top three, was the crop actually grown, compared with simple baselines.
val.m3_reason: First guess right {{a}}, in the top three {{b}}
val.m3_habit: It learns local habit: a common next crop is not necessarily a suitable one.
val.m3_rule: Never shown as high: it predicts habit, not suitability.

money.title: Money: revenue, costs and risk
money.sub: What up to three rotations could earn on this field, what they cost, and how risky they are. Built on the same simulation as your options, with USDA regional prices and costs you can replace with your own.
money.support: This supports your own budget and your adviser. It does not replace them.
money.loading: Working out the money for this field…
money.unavailable_title: Money is not available for this field
money.pick_help: Pick up to three. Your current rotation is always worked out too, for the comparison.
money.pick_max: Three are picked. Untick one to pick another.
money.crops_help: Filled in with averages for your area. Change any number you know better; the results above update straight away.
money.usda_label: USDA regional average ({{region}}), not your farm
money.usda_label_noregion: USDA regional average, not your farm
money.total_typed: You typed a total, so the lines below are not used. Reset to USDA to go back to the lines.
money.no_usda: No USDA prices or costs for {{crop}} here. Enter your own typical yield, price and operating costs to include it.
money.acres_help: From the field boundary: {{ac}} acres ({{ha}} ha).
money.acres_help_none: No field size came with this field: type yours to see whole-field totals.
money.pump_help: The simulation gives the water each option pumps in each weather year. Leave empty and pumping is not counted.
money.pump_off: Pumping is not counted yet. Add your cost per acre-inch under “Show cost details”.
money.overhead: Include fixed costs (land, machinery, labour, overhead)
money.overhead_help: Off: net return over operating costs, as on the Compare page. On: USDA fixed costs are taken off too; land rent can be changed in each crop's cost lines.
money.losses: Include losses the weather model does not cover (hail, flood, wind…)
money.losses_help: From USDA crop-insurance records for this county; real losses on your field can differ. Drought, heat and in-season frost are already in the weather simulation and are not added twice.
money.losses_none: Crop-insurance loss records could not be loaded for this county, so hail, flood and wind losses are not included.
money.grid_note: {{s}} real weather sequences ({{y0}}–{{y1}}) × {{p}} price years = {{n}} simulated years per option.
money.grid_note_noprice: {{s}} real weather sequences ({{y0}}–{{y1}}), with your prices.

stress_note.prices: Every crop price 20 % lower than the numbers above.
stress_note.drought: Only the driest 20 % of weather sequences: {{n}} of {{s}} (growing-season rain at or below {{mm}} mm).
stress_note.both: The driest 20 % of weather sequences ({{n}} of {{s}}) and every crop price 20 % lower.

money.results_h: What each option could earn on this field
money.range_aria: Bad year {{bad}}, typical {{typ}}, good year {{good}}, per acre a year

loss.none: Chance of losing money in a year: none of the {{n}} simulated years lost money.
loss.rare: Chance of losing money in a year: less than 1 in 40.
loss.one_in: Chance of losing money in a year: about 1 in {{n}}.
loss.k_in_10: Chance of losing money in a year: about {{k}} in 10.
loss.most: Chance of losing money in a year: almost every year, with these numbers.

money.beat: Beats what you grow now in {{k}} years out of 10.
money.be_up: It would earn the same as your current rotation if crop prices rose {{pct}} %.
money.be_down: It would earn the same as your current rotation if crop prices fell {{pct}} %.
money.be_zero: At today's prices it earns about the same as your current rotation.
money.be_ahead: It stays ahead of your current rotation whether prices fall 80 % or double.
money.be_behind: It stays behind your current rotation whether prices fall 80 % or double.
money.worst: Worst year on record here ({{y}} weather): {{v}} per acre.
money.incomplete: Needs your numbers for {{list}} before it can be worked out.
money.base_incomplete: Your current rotation needs numbers too before the options can be compared with it.
money.method: How it is worked out: each option runs through every real weather sequence (NASA POWER, ≈50 km regional weather) and every recent USDA price year. For each pair, net per acre = yield × price − costs, averaged over the rotation's years. Typical is the middle year; bad and good are the 1-in-10 low and high. Observed patterns do not prove a switch will pay.
money.haz_intro: From what actually happened here, with the year it last happened.
money.haz_insured_line: {{cause}}: {{crop}} insurance paid out in {{hit}} of the last {{n}} years, about {{v}} per acre when it did
money.haz_insured_sim: (already in the weather simulation, not added again)
money.haz_none: No records came back for this field.
money.haz_missing: Hazard history is not available from the server yet.
money.use: Use these numbers in the ranking
money.use_help: Writes your yields, prices and operating costs into the ranking, so the Compare page and your plan use them. Cover, pumping and fixed costs stay here.
money.use_done: The ranking now uses your numbers for: {{crops}}.
money.use_cleared: Your numbers match USDA, so the ranking keeps the USDA numbers.
money.go_help: Revenue, costs and risk for your options, with your own prices and costs.

money.stress_hint: Lower prices, drought years, hail and flood losses
money.pick_show: Change which options are compared ({{n}} shown)
money.costs_hint: Seed, fertiliser and other costs, cover crops, pumping, land and machinery
money.no_usda_any: There are no USDA averages for some crops here. Type your own typical yield, price and costs for them; the options that use them appear once those are filled in.

money.per_acre_line: That is {{typ}} per acre a year ({{bad}} in a bad year).

money.field_good: Whole field in a good year: about {{v}}.
money.beat_never: Does not beat what you grow now in the simulated years.
money.beat_always: Beats what you grow now in almost every simulated year.
money.worst_detail: The worst year combines the weather of {{wy}} with the prices of {{py}}.
money.lines_vs_total: The lines add up to {{sum}}. The Compare page uses USDA's yearly total, {{total}}: each line is its own 5-year middle value, so they differ a little.

money.yield_records_other: Your own average of {{count}} years from your records ({{span}}). {{was}}.
